Brings the go build cache under a byte cap by deleting the cache entries that have
gone longest unused, so the entries the next build wants stay and the build stays
warm. Only go's own entries are removed; the cache's bookkeeping files are kept, and a
cache already under its cap is left untouched.

DIR defaults to GOCACHE, else ~/.cache/go-build. The cap defaults to
ERUN_GO_BUILD_CACHE_MAX_BYTES, the value the runtime chart renders (0 means no bound),
else 16 GiB. --dry-run reports how many entries would go without deleting any.

Usage:
  erun trim-cache [DIR] [flags]

Examples:
  erun trim-cache --dry-run
  erun trim-cache --max-bytes 8589934592 ~/.cache/go-build

Flags:
      --dry-run         Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
  -h, --help            help for trim-cache
      --max-bytes int   Cap in bytes (default: ERUN_GO_BUILD_CACHE_MAX_BYTES, else 16 GiB)

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
